title: James Frewin Matchbox - Slide-Out Tray & Strike-to-Ignite

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A card matchbox: thumb slides the inner tray out, then a match is dragged quickly along the side striker strip; it flares, settles into a warm living flame and slowly burns down the stick.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: Two-stage gesture sequence: drag the tray out (or press Enter), then drag a match across the striker quickly (or press Enter again). The strike velocity and the striker-strip contact decide ignition; the flame then lives - flickers, burns down the stick over time.

design_tokens.borders: Cardboard tray edges with printed label face; striker strip as a dark speckled band
design_tokens.elevation: Drawer-slide parallax between tray and sleeve; flame glow as the only volumetric element

interactive_mechanics: Slide-out tray drag with drawer physics
Velocity-gated strike: fast drag along the strip ignites, slow drag does not
Living flame animation that burns down the stick over session time
Full keyboard equivalent: Enter opens tray, Enter again strikes
usability_notes: A model two-step ritual component: each physical sub-action maps to one gesture AND one key, so the metaphor never blocks input. The velocity gate teaches the 'quick strike' through failure (a lazy drag just scuffs) - keep a visible hint so users connect drag speed to ignition. Flame states could serve as session or progress indicators. Source: component page self-documentation.
